cases.name: 1952 Washington, D.C., UFO incident
cases.description: Series of UFO sightings and unknown radar returns over Washington, D.C., from July 12 to 29, 1952, centred on Washington National Airport and Andrews Air Force Base.

cases.name: 1976 Tehran UFO incident
cases.description: 19 September 1976 radar and visual sighting of an unidentified object over Tehran, Iran, during which two Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 interceptors reported instrument and communications failures.

cases.name: 1984 Hudson Valley UFO sightings
cases.description: Wave of UFO reports in 1983-1984 across the Hudson Valley of New York and western Connecticut, attributed by state police to light planes flying in formation.

cases.name: 2006 O'Hare International Airport UFO sighting
cases.description: 7 November 2006 report by United Airlines employees of a metallic, saucer-shaped object hovering over Gate C-17 at Chicago O'Hare International Airport.

cases.name: 2022–2023 Middle East and Mediterranean Sea UAP incident
cases.description: Three UAP reports filed by theater UAV operators after missions in the Middle East and the Mediterranean Sea in 2022 and 2023, in which infrared video seemed to show an atmospheric wake or anomalous propulsion; resolved by AARO as prosaic aircraft with a sensor artifact.

cases.name: 2023 Eglin Air Force Base UAP incident
cases.description: A military pilot's 26 January 2023 report of four potential UAP in the Eglin Air Force Base training range off Florida, resolved by AARO as very likely a balloon.

cases.name: Pentagon UFO videos

sources.title: AARO Go Fast Case Resolution Card with Appendix

cases.description: The January 2015 "Go Fast" incident, in which a U.S. Navy F/A-18F recorded an object on FLIR off the coast of Florida, as analysed and resolved by AARO in February 2025.

cases.name: AARO Historical Record Report, Volume 1
cases.description: February 2024 Department of Defense / AARO report reviewing the historical record of U.S. Government involvement with UAP since 1945.

cases.name: 2013 Aguadilla UAP incident

sources.title: AARO Puerto Rico Case Resolution Card

cases.description: Two objects recorded on infrared video by a U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircraft over Rafael Hernandez Airport near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, on April 26, 2013, which AARO resolved in March 2025 as probably a pair of sky lanterns.

cases.name: 2017 Southeast Asia UAP incident

sources.title: AARO Case Resolution of 'Southeast Asia Triangles'

cases.description: Six dark triangular objects in a formation seen in satellite imagery of Southeast Asia dated 30 August 2017, flagged as potentially anomalous and resolved by AARO as fishing nets.

cases.name: 2021 Western United States UAP incident

sources.title: AARO Case Resolution of 'Western United States'

cases.description: Military personnel in 2021 reported five equidistant lights on an infrared sensor as a potential incursion into restricted military airspace in the western United States; resolved by AARO as commercial aircraft up to 300 nautical miles away.

cases.name: Antônio Vilas-Boas
cases.description: 1957 claim by Brazilian farmer Antônio Vilas-Boas that he was taken aboard a landed craft by humanoids near São Francisco de Sales.

cases.name: Ariel School UFO incident
cases.description: 16 September 1994 report by 62 pupils of Ariel School near Ruwa, Zimbabwe, of silver objects landing beside the school and beings dressed in black.

cases.name: Aztec crashed saucer hoax
cases.description: Allegation that a flying saucer crashed near Aztec, New Mexico in 1948, exposed in 1952 as a hoax by two con men.

cases.name: Barney and Betty Hill incident
cases.description: Alleged abduction of Barney and Betty Hill by extraterrestrials in rural New Hampshire on 19-20 September 1961.

cases.name: Battle of Los Angeles
cases.description: Rumored Japanese air attack and anti-aircraft barrage over Los Angeles on the night of 24-25 February 1942, later featured in UFO conspiracy theories.

cases.name: Belgian UFO wave
cases.description: Series of sightings of triangular UFOs in Belgium from 29 November 1989 to April 1990, peaking with an F-16 scramble on 30 March 1990.

cases.name: Cash–Landrum incident
cases.description: 29 December 1980 report by Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum of a flame-emitting diamond-shaped object and helicopters near Dayton, Texas, followed by health claims and a dismissed lawsuit.

cases.name: Chiles-Whitted UFO encounter
cases.description: July 24, 1948 sighting by two Eastern Air Lines pilots of a glowing object near Montgomery, Alabama, later attributed to a meteor.

cases.name: David Grusch UFO whistleblower claims
cases.description: Claims made public in June 2023 by former USAF intelligence officer David Grusch that the U.S. government runs secret programs recovering and reverse engineering 'non-human' spacecraft and their dead pilots.

cases.name: Disappearance of Frederick Valentich
cases.description: 1978 disappearance of an Australian pilot over Bass Strait after he radioed that an unidentified aircraft was accompanying him.

cases.name: Exeter incident
cases.description: UFO sighting on September 3, 1965 in Kensington near Exeter, New Hampshire, by a teenager and two police officers.

cases.name: Falcon Lake Incident
cases.description: Alleged UFO encounter on 20 May 1967 at Falcon Lake, Manitoba, in which lone witness Steve Michalak claimed he was burned by a landed craft's exhaust.

cases.name: Felix Moncla
cases.description: 23 November 1953 disappearance of USAF pilot Felix Moncla and his F-89C Scorpion over Lake Superior while intercepting an unidentified radar target.

cases.name: Flatwoods monster
cases.description: Alleged humanoid reported by a group of local residents in Flatwoods, West Virginia, on September 12, 1952 after a bright light crossed the night sky.

cases.name: Ghost rockets
cases.description: Wave of rocket- or missile-shaped unidentified flying objects sighted in 1946, primarily over Sweden and other Scandinavian countries.

cases.name: Gorman dogfight
cases.description: 1 October 1948 incident in which National Guard pilot George F. Gorman chased a blinking ball of light over Fargo, North Dakota.

cases.name: Gulf Breeze UFO incident
cases.description: Series of claimed UFO sightings in Gulf Breeze, Florida, in late 1987 and early 1988 that began with photographs by contractor Ed Walters, widely suspected to be a hoax.

cases.name: House Oversight UAP hearing, July 2023

sources.title: House Oversight hearing: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency
sources.publisher: US House Committee on Oversight and Accountability

cases.description: 26 July 2023 hearing of the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs on UAP (opening statements and first two witness statements).

cases.name: House Oversight UAP hearing, November 2024

sources.title: House Oversight joint hearing: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth
sources.publisher: US House Committee on Oversight and Accountability

cases.description: Joint hearing of two House Oversight subcommittees on unidentified anomalous phenomena, held 13 November 2024.

cases.name: Japan Air Lines Cargo Flight 1628
cases.description: 17 November 1986 UFO sighting reported by the captain of a Japan Air Lines Boeing 747-200 cargo flight over eastern Alaska.

cases.name: Kaikōura lights
cases.description: Series of UFO sightings in December 1978 above the Kaikōura mountain ranges, New Zealand, including lights filmed from a Safe Air cargo plane.

cases.name: Kecksburg UFO incident
cases.description: 9 December 1965 fireball seen over six U.S. states and Canada, with claims that an object crashed in woods at Kecksburg, Pennsylvania.

cases.name: Kelly–Hopkinsville encounter
cases.description: Claimed 1955 close encounter in which a Kentucky farm family said small creatures from a spaceship besieged their farmhouse.

cases.name: Kenneth Arnold UFO sighting
cases.description: 24 June 1947 sighting by private pilot Kenneth Arnold of nine shiny objects flying past Mount Rainier, Washington, which gave rise to the term 'flying saucer'.

cases.name: Lakenheath-Bentwaters incident
cases.description: Series of radar and visual contacts with unidentified objects over airbases in eastern England on the night of 13-14 August 1956.

cases.name: Levelland UFO case
cases.description: UFOs reportedly seen around highways near Levelland, Texas on 2-3 November 1957, with numerous reports of stalled vehicle engines and lights.

cases.name: Lonnie Zamora incident
cases.description: Alleged 1964 UFO sighting near Socorro, New Mexico, in which police officer Lonnie Zamora claimed to see two figures beside an egg shaped object that rose on a flame.

cases.name: Lubbock Lights
cases.description: Formation of lights seen over Lubbock, Texas in August and September 1951, photographed by Carl Hart, Jr. and investigated by the U.S. Air Force.

cases.name: Malmstrom UFO incident
cases.description: Claims, first made publicly in 1996, that a 1967 shutdown of nuclear missiles at Echo Flight, Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, was connected to a UFO sighting.

cases.name: Manises UFO incident
cases.description: 11 November 1979 incident in which a Spanish commercial flight made an emergency landing at Manises Airport after its crew reported red lights, followed by a Spanish Air Force Mirage F1 pursuit.

cases.name: Mantell UFO incident
cases.description: 7 January 1948 fatal crash of Kentucky Air National Guard pilot Thomas F. Mantell while pursuing an unidentified flying object over Kentucky.

cases.name: Mariana UFO film
cases.description: 1950 sighting and 16 mm film of two bright objects over Great Falls, Montana by Nick Mariana.

cases.name: Maury Island incident
cases.description: Alleged June 21, 1947 UFO sighting over Maury Island, Washington, widely regarded as a hoax.

cases.name: McMinnville UFO photographs
cases.description: Two photographs of an alleged disk-shaped UFO taken by Paul Trent on a farm near McMinnville, Oregon, on 11 May 1950.

cases.name: Michigan "swamp gas" UFO reports
cases.description: Two mass UFO sightings on 20-21 March 1966 near Dexter and Hillsdale College, Michigan, amid a wider flap, attributed to swamp gas by Air Force investigator J. Allen Hynek.

cases.name: ODNI Preliminary Assessment, 2021

sources.title: Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
sources.publisher: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

cases.description: Unclassified 25 June 2021 ODNI preliminary report to Congress on unidentified aerial phenomena and the work of the UAP Task Force.

cases.name: Pascagoula incident
cases.description: Alleged 1973 close encounter in which Charles Hickson and Calvin Parker claimed they were taken aboard a UFO and examined while fishing near Pascagoula, Mississippi.

cases.name: Petrozavodsk phenomenon
cases.description: Series of luminous aerial events on 20 September 1977 reported from Denmark and Finland across the Soviet Union, named for a glowing 'jellyfish' object over Petrozavodsk.

cases.name: Phoenix Lights
cases.description: Widely sighted lights over Arizona and Nevada on March 13, 1997, comprising a triangular formation of lights and a later row of stationary lights near Phoenix.

cases.name: Rendlesham Forest incident
cases.description: Series of reported sightings of unexplained lights near Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk, England, in December 1980, linked with alleged UFO landings.

cases.name: Robert Taylor incident
cases.description: Claimed 9 November 1979 encounter of forester Robert Taylor with a 'flying dome' on Dechmont Law, Livingston, Scotland, recorded by police as an assault.

cases.name: Roswell incident
cases.description: Recovery in 1947 of balloon debris from a ranch near Roswell, New Mexico, which later became the basis for conspiracy theories about a crashed extraterrestrial spacecraft.

cases.name: Shag Harbour UFO incident
cases.description: Reported impact of a large, unknown object into waters near Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia, on 4 October 1967.

cases.name: Trans-en-Provence case
cases.description: Alleged 8 January 1981 landing of a saucer-shaped object on a farmer's property outside Trans-en-Provence, France, said to have left physical traces on the ground.

cases.name: Travis Walton incident
cases.description: Alleged alien abduction of forestry worker Travis Walton on November 5, 1975, near Heber, Arizona, after which he was missing for five days.

cases.name: Val Johnson incident
cases.description: Alleged 1979 UFO encounter in Marshall County, Minnesota, reported by Deputy Sheriff Val Johnson.

cases.name: Varginha UFO incident
cases.description: Series of events in 1996 in which residents of Varginha, Brazil, claimed to have seen strange humanoids and at least one UFO.

cases.name: Voronezh UFO incident
cases.description: Alleged sighting of a UFO and alien beings reported by a group of children in Voronezh, Soviet Union, on September 27, 1989, publicized by TASS.

cases.name: Westall UFO
cases.description: Reported sighting on 6 April 1966 of a flying object by students and teachers of Westall High School in Melbourne, Australia.

ev.q: The 1952 UFO flap was an unprecedented rash of media attention to unidentified flying object reports during the summer of 1952 that culminated with reports of sightings over Washington, D.C.

ev.q:
known as thermal
crossover. When a sensor fails to discriminate a target from its environment, the object can
seem to vanish or intermittently disappear and reappear.³

Rather, the sensor could
not distinguish the objects from their environment due to a lack of thermal contrast between
them and the ocean.

Thermal imaging can fail to differentiate a target object from the background when its thermal
signature is virtually identical to the surrounding environment to be distinct, known as thermal
crossover.
